second_reasoning: The select-event path that re-runs the slash menu predates the graft; GraphQL blame at the graft attributes the `updateSlashMenu` call in `handleSelect` to f8550bc11d4d (#122425), whose diff shows it added that line to a listener that previously only updated the skill menu, while the arg branch already reset `slashMenuIndex = 0`. Later Solid-store refactors (3c099685538f) and the command-mode-only sibling fix 788093dbc81f (#193758) carried the reset unchanged. Medium because I did not run the pre-#122425 UI to confirm the arg highlight survived keyboard selection there, though the listener had no slash-menu call before.

The on-exit-cwd check lived only in resolveDirectSchedule (from the on-exit feature, 68bfa42b) and in create; the stream-metadata edit path that bypasses it was introduced in 98742bc2c7f2 (#112387), whose diff shows the new early return placed before resolveDirectSchedule with the check left in place. The path never validated the flag pair from its introduction, so this is never-worked rather than a regression; later commits only changed error types and trimming.

resolveNodeRuntimeExecutable was introduced in #145688 to find a real Node under Bun, and both its fast path and probe only excluded Bun and checked a flag, never the Node version; later commits (#183120, #183493) moved the probe into a generated asset without changing the predicate. The defect therefore shipped with the resolver; medium confidence because it only bites once helper code uses syntax the stray old Node lacks, which could be read as latent.

The access section was introduced in #135840 with an explicit inspectionError branch that showed a retry error instead of the skeleton, so failure was handled. #142713 (unify installed plugin detail tabs) removed that branch from renderAccess and kept the `!props.inspection` skeleton, so a failed inspection rendered as permanent loading; later refactors (#149246, #150234, #150235, #168758) carried the `!inspection -> loading` condition forward unchanged until this fix.

The pinned 0.164.0 runtime and its generated schemas were correct when adopted (#181823); they became insufficient because OpenAI's backend gates new models by Codex client version and the upstream protocol added new shapes (audio fileId), both external changes. No in-repo commit broke working behavior, so this is latent with no in-repo trigger; it could also be read as a routine dependency bump.

The removed condition was a deliberate rule added in #199051, documented by the comment 'A remembered Favorites tab opens only while it holds the selected model' and asserted by its test ('An unstarred selection opens its own provider'). The fix reverses that product rule and updates docs accordingly, so it is a behavior change rather than a defect.

Issue #195636 came from code review and reports only a retained destroyed Activity; the PR keeps the existing foreground admission that already stopped captures from binding to a stale owner, and the only device evidence is a trace showing the reference held until the next attach, with no reported failure. The strong `lifecycleOwner = owner` reference goes back past the January 2026 package renames to the original Android node code, so no introducing commit could be pinned. A stricter reader could call it a never-worked memory leak, but with no observed user failure and no traceable cause, I classify it as leak hardening.

The PR itself frames this as a work-count (style pass) improvement with no claimed latency or visible behavior change, and no regression from a faster prior state is shown; the identity comparison and inline inert bindings have been that way since the Solid port/review-controls commits. Under the rubric this is a performance improvement of code that was never slower before, so not-a-defect.

Issue #168784 shows explicit compile always published a fresh but identical snapshot; the compiled output stayed correct and the documented reuse rule only covered source synchronization, so explicit-compile reuse is a new optimization that removes churn rather than a repair of broken behavior. No commit is shown to have removed earlier reuse in the explicit path (the blame candidates are type/refactor cleanups); if one treats the churn as a defect it would be never-worked in the original compiled-cache publication design, which I could not pin to a commit.

SQLite accepts these escapes, so the failure exists only on the PostgreSQL path, which was created by #171545 (93e8fe35376) adding `::jsonb` casts in jsonPathValue and wiring the transcript readers to it; the edge case was never handled there, and #183560 later added the guard for some readers but not these. Medium rather than high because the NUL full-text index failure and a few guarded readers trace to sibling Postgres-port commits (e.g. #174786, #183560), not only #171545.

Before #194885, every read checkpointed guest changes and then read the canonical file, so a save followed by a read returned the saved bytes and host sessions read canonical files. #194885 (merged about 1.5 hours before this fix, which names it) switched reads to the live private checkout for any worktree session without synchronizing saves into that checkout; I read both diffs in session-file-read.ts and sessions-files.ts.

At 455e84f77694's tree Twilio playTts already sent Say followed by Gather, and speakInitialMessage did not call startListening afterward; that commit (aimed at Telnyx) added the conversation-mode startListening for every non-streaming provider including Twilio, which is the greeting loss reported in #158262. The second symptom (5-second Gather default timeout and continueCall's speak-then-startListening) is older code that never handled silence, so the fix mixes a regression with a never-worked part; medium confidence because I did not exhaustively rule out other pre-April startListening callers.

Visitor Access (older than the graft) always captured its config at registration, so any config edit required plugin replacement; that was fine until the reload machinery evolved to gate new agent work behind exclusive replacement that drains held turns (e.g. 88fff4ed5ae, 2d5c68187a3, 62e0b2b7fcf), turning a limit edit into a 60 s blocked window. No single commit broke a previously working path that I can quote, and the drain gating is deliberate design, so this is a long-standing plugin contract exposed by changes outside it rather than a regression; I could not pin one trigger commit.

GraphQL blame of the fix parent puts the `options[key].slice(0, 6)` line on deslop refactor 8bfe139a13b, whose diff shows it replaced an equivalent `for (const val of values.slice(0, 6))` slice-then-filter loop; that came from split refactor 68dbbc7c5ff, which moved code from ui/src/ui/views/usage.ts where the cap-before-match lines blame to 8a352c8f9df, the commit that introduced the usage dashboard. The cap-before-match ordering was present from the start, so the bug shipped with the feature.

The review was correctly refused before and after the change; no review runs in either case and no behavior, authority or delivery changes. The fix only refines the log reason code for operators, which is a diagnostics/copy improvement rather than a defect with a broken behavior.

The synchronous capture-root creation on the main thread was a long-standing design (the parent allocation callback already existed before the blame candidates, e.g. dfb91dc29046 only moved worker-side root bookkeeping), and it is normally fast; it stalled only when the host filesystem (btrfs) blocked in wait_current_trans during a Team incident. No commit made this path slower, so it is environment-exposed latent behavior rather than a regression; the PR accepts higher total cost to keep the event loop free.

The linked issue #191925 is a feature request ('Improve Gateway downtime holding and retry guidance') that states current source already retains the loaded Control UI and draft; the remaining work is described as presentation and guidance. This is a UX redesign, not a fix for behavior that previously worked or shipped broken.

Blame puts the removed line on e29577b7d7df, which created people-error.ts; git grep at that commit shows packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/authority/apply.ts already emitting limit_reached for invite count and lifetime limits, so the misleading guidance shipped with the page.

Blame of all removed lines points to 58b88a8b0a80, whose diff adds the ProgressRuntime component including the .slice(0, 240) detail; the feature and the unsafe cut shipped together. formatUiExternalText only trims and redacts, so nothing upstream made the slice safe.

The adapter's get_window_state request (older than the graft, last adjusted by 371791b9d6be for include_screenshot) relied on CUA Driver's default tree format, which worked until CUA 0.37 changed that default to Markdown. The in-repo exposure is the dependency refresh 70134e42285 (#188576), whose package.json diff moves @trycua/cua-driver from 0.36.0 to 0.37.0; that is an external API change, not a code regression, so latent with that commit as trigger.

Blame of the removed lines points to bb6bb777af31 (#157349), whose diff adds skippedFloodResponse with the '; request not sent)' description and routes sendChatAction through the replaceable skip path; the typing call sites in bot-message-context.ts were already wrapped in withTelegramApiErrorLogging(operation: "sendChatAction"), so every skipped typing logged an ERROR from the day the hold-back feature shipped. The same PR intended a single WARN per flood, so the per-request ERROR is a defect of that introduction, not a later regression.

The removed `signal: params?.signal` line was added by 2640154bcf80 (#137071), whose diff converts probeClaudeCliAuthStatus from a blocking spawnSync (which callers could not cancel and whose timeout only sent a SIGTERM that Claude Code defers) to the async runner with the caller's signal and process-tree kill (SIGTERM then SIGKILL 300 ms later). That makes a cancelled discovery kill the refresh and orphan .oauth_refresh.lock; before it, a cancelled caller could not kill the probe. Medium because I could not confirm that the Claude Code version current in September 2026 already refreshed tokens under the lock inside `auth status`; if that came later the case would be latent.

The PR itself shows unpatched 2026.10.9 completed the same callback and token exchange under the old wording, so login worked in every case; the change is status copy plus skipping a 16-second wait in the bind-failure case, where pasting the redirect URL already completed sign-in. The removed lines are mostly older than the graft, with only refactors after it (2d5b670129b8, b10d3f701143), and the wording has been reworked many times in the file's history, so there is no specific breaking commit; I treat it as a UX and copy improvement, not a defect.

The greeting builder and onboarding opening prompt were introduced in #175291 (413d2fc) with English-only text and no locale input; git log shows agent-onboarding.ts was untouched between that commit and the fix, so the English-only greeting shipped with the feature rather than being broken later. Confidence is medium because localizing the greeting could also be read as a feature extension rather than a defect, though the Control UI is localized into 23 languages and the fix is titled and framed as a fix.

The PR describes a speedup: the existing pipeline always re-encoded MOV playback renditions and returned 'preparing' immediately by design, and nothing indicates it was ever faster before. This is a performance improvement of code that was never slower than before, so not-a-defect; blame points only at a UI refactor and pre-graft code with no breaking change.

The harness helper was extracted in #159375 (42e53a49) from Codex session-history.ts, where the budget x 8 cap was first added by #149520 (83f94849); at that commit openModelContextAsync limits were optional and the Codex read previously passed none, so whole history was retained until compaction. The fix's mutation test (restoring 128_000 x 8 reproduces the 25-of-43 cut) matches that line. Medium rather than high because the cap was a deliberate memory bound whose bytes-per-token assumption failed for reasoning and image payloads, so one could also read it as a flawed design shipped with the bound.

Issue #168743 reports the 4008 refusal loop starting 2026-10-03, days after #159860 (28e16ee, 2026-09-28) created ControlUINativeGatewayAuthMessageHandler.swift and DashboardNativeGatewayAuth.swift (git log shows no earlier commits) and made the refusal retryable in the UI client; close handling already only called stopLoading, which never unloaded the committed page. So the refusal loop for closed windows shipped with the native auth bridge rather than being introduced later. Medium because I could not confirm exactly which bridge condition fails after close (likely hasCurrentBrowserSession after nativeBrowser.dispose).

The generic fallback and the first-write-wins `failure ??=` recording for scheduled session-target turns arrived together in #178764 (3d2f7ca), which first ran scheduled conversation work through this session-event handoff; later commits (#182262 moved the fallback into settleSessionEventTurn, #192550 added result.cause only for the terminal outcome) kept the generic text winning for the recorded error. I did not confirm how the incident's refusal reached the recorded failure at 3d2f7ca (thrown error vs operation result), nor whether the pre-3d2f7ca cron path recorded the real cause, so confidence is low.

The candidate state snapshot (d1a69c0b209, 2026-09-06) predates file-backed cold archives, which arrived in aa0ad4c7804 (2026-09-11) with external payload files and backup support but no change to update-candidate-state.ts; the fix's PR confirms no cold-file copy ever ran in the snapshot. I treat the gap as shipped with the cold-archive feature rather than a later regression; it could also be read as latent with that commit as trigger, and I did not confirm which Doctor path first read the missing payloads in rehearsal.

Person-Activity FORBIDDEN denials for guests were introduced by 5d3e157432a (#191978), whose UI part only cleared rows on FORBIDDEN and did not stop the existing invalidate/refresh paths from re-reading the denied query, so the flicker shipped with that feature. I confirmed the owner's history and the parent's invalidate() still refreshing on any session change; earlier refactors (10c95d1a605 etc.) predate the denial state, so they are not the cause.

The completion component was created in 18136c960eaf (#198133) deliberately rendering `<Icon name="bot" />` and the plain label; nothing broke or misbehaved, and the fix is a visual-consistency polish of that design rather than a repair of a failure. I read the introducing file's diff and the one-file fix; I classify it as a presentation/product change, though one could argue it as a never-worked inconsistency in 18136c960eaf.

The diagnostics timeline writer batches events and flushes on a later setImmediate turn, which is fine for its own contract; it only became wrong once benchmark/perf collectors (scripts/bench-*, scripts/perf/*) used /readyz as the end of their evidence window. The batching code is older than the history I could search (no in-repo commit found by path-limited search), the change is a forward-port from release/2026.10.10 whose own message names no cause, and the fix notes main's readiness ordering differs from the release branch, so I name no cause or trigger commit.

The removed `loadedCard.outputText === undefined` condition and the unconditional actions block trace back through the Solid refactors (#176599, #179556) and the Lit-to-Solid migration (#168739) unchanged to the original full-output recovery component added in fd77e9230188 (#153542). That diff contains both the same undefined-text-means-unavailable check and the actions rendered for any non-loading state, so non-text results were mislabeled from the start; the fix PR notes image-only MCP results come from existing MCP conversion, not a later change.

GraphQL blame shows the removed `sandbox list --limit ... --offset ... --output json` phase lookup came from ac157b3af0cd (#115058, 2026-07-28), written against the OpenShell CLI current at the time; the fix PR states these CLI contracts were removed by OpenShell v0.1.3, an external tool change. The in-repo exposure is the dependency refresh 0320b94b6958 (#174410), which moved the CI pin from v0.1.2 to v0.1.3, so I record it as trigger rather than cause; I could not independently verify the upstream flag removal beyond the PR's baseline CI evidence.

The exact check `generationOwner.requiredGeneration !== snapshot.sharedGeneration` dates from 961f5c0b7099 (#166553), where it guarded short-lived Control UI restart recovery and the trusted-proxy generation already hashed proxy admission settings (ws-shared-generation.ts unchanged in substance since); refusing recovery there with 'start a new user turn' was a defensible conservative policy. d74a4aeb7d6 (#176422) made long-lived cron jobs retain operator sources and restore through the same restoreGatewayOperatorSource path, relying on authority surviving proxy-policy changes that the restore code never promised, so I classify it latent with that commit as trigger; a reader could also defend never-worked at d74a4aeb7d6.

The removed line `disposition: "intentional_non_delivery"` in sourceOwnerChangedResult predates the graft (GraphQL blame points only to the c61ba3ea extraction refactor, which moved the existing literal unchanged), and its name shows a deliberate design that source-lifecycle refusals are silent non-delivery. The fix reverses that policy, following the same direction as #200760 (714129c06), which two days earlier deleted other deliberate post-completion refusals; no commit broke a working behavior, so this is a product/policy change rather than a regression. A reader treating the original design as a defect could call it never-worked, but its introducing commit is older than the graft and was not found.

GraphQL blame shows the image max-count of 10 came from the extension's introduction #19424 (bfc97363), whose ShareViewController capped attachments at 3 and never sent videos; the movie key was added by #20308 (c2d12b7e) while videos were still unsupported. The activation rule and send capability were mismatched from the start; #106513 (6e8df6c0) later turned the silent truncation into a blocked Send, which made the mismatch obvious but did not create it. Confidence is medium because the visible blocked-sheet symptom dates to #106513 and the video half to #20308.

All removed lines blame to #188497 (29503e14), which introduced the interrupted-updater recovery path, restoreRepairGateway and its ownership throw; its diff shows the stop check gated on `updaterStopped` and done only once, and the terminal runtime path switched only after finalization, which are exactly the three defects the fix names. No intermediate commit changed these lines, so the defects shipped with the feature.

Before #196662 (10d67445), command checkpoints paused the guest and captured directly into Git, which is the behavior this fix restores; #196662 introduced the per-checkpoint btrfs snapshot and removal, and #196727 (d7f90ec3) only narrowed it to large or slow workspaces such as the production one. The fix cites a production incident of Gateway-wide stalls attributed to those snapshots. Confidence is medium because #196662 was a deliberate pause-versus-I/O trade-off and the btrfs mechanism was inferred, not measured natively.

At the fix parent, getSharedGatewayContextResolver throws 'incompatible Gateway bindings: bound and unbound owners' for a mixed batch, and visible spawn / sessions_send follow-up registration never passed gatewayContextResolver, so mixed batches failed whole; this is an interaction between batch settlement, restoration (which drops in-memory bindings) and paths that never captured a binding. The throw predates the file's creation in c69b8b98 (#153508, a large move) and I could not trace the introducing commit or establish that mixed batches ever worked, and the blame candidates (deslop refactor, #163195, #129535, #198807) touch peripheral lines rather than the failing mechanism.

The bug is that retiring the old socket's startup credentials before reconnect changed the auth value (legacyCredentials) and so looked like a credential change, replacing the WebView; the legacyCredentials field inside the Equatable nativeDevice case and the socket retirement logic both arrived in #159860 (GraphQL blame of line 57 and the API patch confirm), which handled only the reconnect-before-retirement order. The later #161464 added the retirement-after-reconnect test only; the retirement-first ordering failed on base per the PR, and I found no evidence it ever worked, so never-worked with medium confidence since the exact comparison lines in DashboardManager could not be read locally.

The defect half (detailed replies rejected, empty partial results) comes from the schema maxItems limits that shipped with the plugin in c50ff4fbe541 (#173964), which created portable.ts with these schemas and the unlimited extraction prompt (blame of the prompt and schema lines points there and the file history starts there). The UI half (removing the header button/bar and inline card) is a product decision layered on newer pane commits; I classed the fix by its defect part, with medium confidence because over-limit replies depend on model behavior.

Before #193548 the age-based sweep bounded and expired the plaintext archive cache; #193548 (an hour before this fix) removed the writer and the sweep without a migration, so caches already on disk were never reclaimed, which is exactly what the fix's PR states. I read the #193548 diff of archive-compression.ts and confirmed the removed sweep lines; the fix adds the missing one-time Doctor cleanup.

#172026 introduced the loopback bridge for configured MCP on managed Claude CLI turns and deliberately passed `requesterSenderId: undefined`, documenting that requester-scoped servers are not offered; the fix adds them. Before #172026 the native Claude CLI path also never carried requester-scoped servers (native projection resolves OAuth with operator identity and omits unavailable servers; docs say requester-scoped servers never enter harness-native config), so this capability never worked on Claude CLI rather than regressing; medium confidence because the omission was a documented choice and could be read as a feature gap.

Per issue #203124 and PR #203177, state metadata reads pass a reduced worker environment ({OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, ...} from openclaw-state-worker-context.capture.ts) to the read-only worker, which has used caller env since September (blame 71a1d0d2060/a06612710e6); the child then re-runs SQLite selection without the env-only library path. That code worked for Node and for Homebrew-discovered libraries (fixed paths), and broke only once the library came solely from OPENCLAW_SQLITE_LIBRARY, as in the macOS app's bundled Bun runtime; I found no single commit that removed a previously working handoff despite the 'restore' title, so I classify it as latent with no identified trigger (an alternative reading is never-worked from 757e482ab646, which added the env override and forwarded it only to the KNN child).

The readers that drop queued input on any assertCurrent throw predate the outage notion (the followup runner already consumed input on any throw before #200213, which only made the drop visible as 'withheld'); dropping became wrong when #198245 introduced the GatewayOperatorAccessUnavailableError contract that a policy outage is non-terminal, without updating the queued-input readers (#198729 then patched only some steer/mailbox paths). So the outage-preservation behavior never worked for queued followups; medium because the defect is an incomplete cutover of the introducing change rather than a single bad line.

The production diff only changes error text; all revocation checks are unchanged, and the PR itself states the investigation found no stale-authority defect and that the triggering revocation remains unattributed. That is a copy/guidance change, so not-a-defect; no cause was sought.
